overstatement_check: Mild. 'Both ... independently found ... routinely circumvented' attributes UK AISI's word 'routinely' to both institutes; US AISI's finding was that safeguards were circumvented 'in most cases' against a series of publicly available jailbreaks. 'Demonstrating a persistent vulnerability' is editorial; the blog says results are 'consistent with prior research on the vulnerability of other AI systems'. Also both institutes tested only 'the version of the safeguards that [they] tested' (built-in model safeguards), a qualifier the Finding drops.
notes: Most serious issue in the batch: Key Quote is unfindable in the cited source or the underlying technical report and must be swapped for the proposed verbatim sentence. Blog also cautions that safeguard results 'cannot on their own determine the model's risks' and that what counts as harmful is subjective - a hostile reviewer could cite this as missing context. Access type pre-deployment confirmed ('findings were shared with Anthropic before the model was publicly released').

overstatement_check: Moderate. 'Outperforming' overstates confidence: the blog explicitly warns 'smaller differences in model performance presented below may fall within the margins of error for these tests', and the technical report shows this is Pass@10 on only 14 apprentice-level tasks (36% vs 29% is roughly a one-task difference); the report elsewhere notes a related apprentice-level subset difference is 'within the margin of error'. Recommend 'compared to' instead of 'outperforming'.
notes: Selective emphasis a hostile reviewer would catch: the same blog section reports US AISI's cyber result where the upgraded model UNDERPERFORMED the best reference (32.5% vs 35% on 40 Cybench CTF challenges); quoting only the favorable UK number invites a cherry-picking charge. Also unstated: metric is Pass@10, and the 36% applies to the 14 apprentice-level tasks within the 47-challenge UK suite, not to all 47.
